long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Taipei, Yin joined the companies established by his family before creating a construction arm two years later. He later earned graduate business degrees from National Taiwan University and National Chengchi University. Although not formally trained as an engineer, he served as chairman, chief engineer and research director, developing automated precast and reinforcement methods that produced hundreds of patents and international honours.

Education and research became another strand of Yin's legacy. In 2012 he committed NT$3 billion to establish the Tang Prize, whose four categories recognize sustainable development, biopharmaceutical science, Sinology and the rule of law. The foundation says his wider scholarship programmes supported more than 163,000 students. Yin died in Taipei in May 2026.
